clue.text: Sparkling wine in the bottom of picnic baskets

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter, here the end of the word picnic

parts.note: hampers are large lidded baskets, often for picnic food

explanation.surface: Bubbly stowed at the bottom of the picnic baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is British slang for champagne, the best-known sparkling wine.

clue.text: Bug firstly cleared Internet cache and, finally, deleted data

indicators.note: firstly asks for the opening letter of each of the four words that follow
finally asks for the closing letter of each of the last two words

explanation.surface: A computer bug wiping a browser cache and losing data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like a software fault, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a chirping insect, and bug is a common term for any insect.

clue.text: A large lady jogging from dawn to dusk?

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: jogging jolts something about, so the letters of lady are shaken up

explanation.surface: Pictures a big woman out running from morning till night.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting the whole time between sunrise and sunset, through the entire day.

clue.text: Musician's support includes piano

indicators.note: includes means the support word contains the piano letter within it

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A musician's stand is said to hold a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes or a pipe, so is a type of musician.

clue.text: It helps you brown a roll on the outside

indicators.note: the roll word sits on the outside, so the letter A goes into it

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget that crisps up a bread roll's crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' reads as bread but means a list of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting tin or oven is used to cook meat until it is browned.

clue.text: A piece of sausage has more than sufficient taste

indicators.note: a piece of the word sausage is taken as its opening letter

parts.note: ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: Someone notes a bit of sausage is plenty to get the flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to try a little of it, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: A girl who likes explorations into kinky love

parts.note: Dora the Explorer is a children's cartoon heroine

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of into are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Suggests a young woman fond of adventure turns to unusual romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep, devoted affection, a synonym for love.

clue.text: Compound to go behind a military building

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure or compound for animals
to tag on is to follow behind someone

explanation.surface: Directions to walk round the back of an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like part of the military setting, but it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense in Virginia.

clue.text: Cook vehemently cutting my position as last batsman

indicators.note: to cook is to falsify or rework, so the letters of vehemently are rearranged
cutting means the letters of my are cut out of the mix

explanation.surface: A cricketer furiously protests at being dropped down the batting order.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange VEHEMENTLY after removing M and Y. In cricket a side has eleven batsmen, so the last one bats at number eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh place in a cricket batting order is the final one, the tail-ender's slot.

clue.text: A group of unemotional acts?

parts.note: someone cold shows no feeling
a stage play is made up of acts, so acts stand for the play

explanation.surface: Asks whether a set of performances could be called heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose link between acts and a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldplay is a British rock band, and a band is a musical group.

clue.text: University head tackles upturn following a decline

indicators.note: the head word takes on, or grips, the university letter, holding it within

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A vice-chancellor deals with a recovery after a slump, like a market report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University head' reads as one title, but they are two pieces: BONCE is British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounce is a recovery, as in prices rising again after they have fallen.

clue.text: National frontrunner absent from Gold Cup venue

indicators.note: the frontrunner is the leading letter, which is dropped from the venue

parts.note: the Gold Cup is a horse race run at Ascot, a racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: The favourite is missing from a famous race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' and 'frontrunner' suggest horse racing (the Grand National), but National is a noun: a citizen of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a native of Scotland, one of its nationals.

clue.text: Accent possibly declared "awful" by reviewer

indicators.note: declared means spoken out loud, so the word for awful is used for how it sounds

parts.note: dire means awful or terrible
a critic reviews books, plays and so on

explanation.surface: A speaker's regional accent is called terrible by a critic.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent DIRE is said like DIA. 'Accent' here means a written mark, not a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic is a mark added to a letter; an acute or grave accent is one example, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: A temptation said to diminish

indicators.note: said signals that the word for temptation is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: bait is a lure or temptation

explanation.surface: Suggests a lure that is claimed to reduce something.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or subside, as a storm does; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Likely to be free from rain

definitions.meaning: a ... chance is a reasonable or likely one

explanation.surface: Sounds like a forecast: probably going to stay dry.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a reasonable prospect and dry, settled weather.

clue.text: Making up a character intended to be heartless

parts.note: the tone of something is its character or quality

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is taken out of the word for intended

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Inventing a figure designed to be cruel, like a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making up' suggests inventing, but here it means making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is reparation for a wrong, as in making up for it.

clue.text: Take a journey away from home to see weird things

parts.note: to trip is to make a short journey
out means not at home

explanation.surface: Advice to travel abroad to see strange sights.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as tourism; the definition is slang for hallucinating on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip out is slang for having drug-induced hallucinations, seeing bizarre visions.

clue.text: Dumb American left after food without tab being sorted

indicators.note: after means the left letter comes at the end, after the rest
without in its old sense of outside, so the food word goes around the sorted letters

parts.note: a meal is food

indicators.note: being sorted means put into a new order, so the letters of tab are rearranged

explanation.surface: A silent American walks out after eating without settling the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumb' suggests silent; here it means stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatball is US slang for a dull, stupid person, a blockhead.

clue.text: Beachside place serving up endless tortillas

indicators.note: serving up suggests dishing out, so the letters are laid out afresh
endless means the final letter of tortillas is dropped

explanation.surface: A seaside café dishing out Mexican flatbreads.
explanation.definitionFit: The littoral is the shore zone of a sea or lake, a coastal region.

clue.text: Good example I found in a record book

indicators.note: the letter I is found in, so placed inside, the record-and-book pieces

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a fine specimen among records and books.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect representative instance, the very model of something.

clue.text: Kid has no time to relax

indicators.note: has no means the time letter is taken away

parts.note: to kid is to tease

explanation.surface: A child too busy to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to relax or slacken, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pipe making a hollow sound

definitions.meaning: a water pipe used for smoking cannabis
the resonant ring of a bell or gong

explanation.surface: A pipe making a dull ringing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a smoker's water pipe and a deep resonant ring.

clue.text: Belt occasionally put on beneath a slip

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so alternate letters of belt are taken

parts.note: under means beneath

explanation.surface: Someone puts a belt on under a petticoat, a dressing mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' reads as an undergarment but means a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is a careless mistake, and a slip is a minor error.

clue.text: Attractive doctor in blue

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A handsome physician in a blue uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person, but it is a verb meaning to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile describes a young woman as sexually appealing, so attractive.

clue.text: Appreciation shown by an actor wanting an award

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the award letters are missing from the actor's name

parts.note: Tom Hanks is a Hollywood actor
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Gratitude shown by a performer who is hoping for an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM (Order of Merit) is a British award; removing it from TOM HANKS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying thank you shows gratitude, so the word expresses appreciation.

clue.text: A certain book regularly talked about sex

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters from talked go round the word for sex
regularly means taking every other letter of talked, starting with the first

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A particular book was often discussed for its sexual content.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a book considered as a published item, as in a publisher's list of titles.

clue.text: Fancy bread is essentially excessive given the money we have

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter, here the middle of excessive

parts.note: our dough is our money, dough being slang for cash

explanation.surface: Complains that posh loaves cost too much on a household budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourdough is an artisan loaf leavened with a fermented starter, a fashionable, upmarket bread.

clue.text: Warehouse often got smashed up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol habitually, so toped means regularly got drunk

explanation.surface: A storage building frequently broken into and wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' looks like breaking, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storage building for goods, a synonym for a warehouse.

clue.text: A grand prophet goes west to get suits

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading from right to left, so the prophet word runs backwards

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A notable prophet heads west to buy some clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' looks like clothing but is the verb: one thing suits, or agrees with, another.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that agrees with you suits you; the verbs are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Backing fixed to an iPod

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Talks of a backing panel attached to a music player.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a proposal means taking it up and supporting it, a sense of approval.

clue.text: Controversial book that's funny and primarily intended to aggravate

parts.note: LOL, laughing out loud, is texting shorthand for something funny

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: Describes a contentious novel as amusing but mainly meant to provoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's 1955 novel about an older man's obsession with a girl caused a lasting scandal.

clue.text: Restrict flying animals

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered through the air and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: An order to keep airborne creatures confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Critters is informal, chiefly American, for creatures in general.
